summary: SimTex's foundational space 4X game and its current DOSBox preservation route.

entries.title: Master of Orion
entries.definitive_edition: Original Master of Orion in the GOG Master of Orion 1+2 package

emulation.emulator: DOSBox included with GOG; DOSBox Staging or 1oom as documented alternatives
emulation.notes: Match sound settings and adjust emulated CPU cycles only as needed; excessive speed can change usability even in a turn-based game.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original DOS assets and behavior with clean scaling and responsive input.

primary.version: Master of Orion 1+2 GOG package, using the original DOS game
primary.why: GOG's DRM-free 1+2 package is the current legal purchase route for the original Master of Orion and runs the DOS release through DOSBox. It preserves the original art, rules, and interface without substituting the separate 2016 reboot.
primary.how_to_play: Install the GOG 1+2 package, launch Master of Orion rather than its sequel, and tune DOSBox cycles only if input or turn processing is abnormally slow. Record game version, DOSBox build, cycles, sound configuration, race, difficulty, and galaxy settings.

all_releases.reason: primary: preserved directly in the current GOG package.
skip: harder modern access and no sourced exclusive game content over the DOS release.

all_releases.platform: Windows / macOS / Linux (GOG Master of Orion 1+2)
all_releases.fidelity: DRM-free DOSBox package containing the original game and Master of Orion II.
all_releases.reason: primary: straightforward current legal access to the original DOS data.

all_releases.fidelity: Community engine recreation requiring legally owned version 1.3 data.
all_releases.reason: fallback only: useful native-engine route, but the GOG DOSBox setup remains the conservative behavior authority.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The GOG DOS release is both complete and faithful. Community engine recreations improve portability but are not required for content.

entries.remaster_caveats: Master of Orion (2016) is a separate reboot, not a remaster or replacement for the 1993 game's rules. 1oom is a community engine recreation and requires the original version 1.3 data.
